patterngeneration.name: Shaders & Patterns: The Book of Shaders
patterngeneration.truth: A fragment shader runs once per pixel. UV is your canvas. Math is your brush. Every function shapes light.
patterngeneration.qfep_connection: Shaders are pure functions mapping coordinates to colors — the most direct expression of mathematical aesthetics. Each pixel independently computes its own reality. In QFEP terms, shaders demonstrate how local rules (per-pixel math) create emergent global patterns — the micro generating the macro.
patterngeneration.formula: color = f(UV, TIME, uniforms) — every pixel independently evaluates the same function
patterngeneration.demonstration: Watch mathematical functions become visual. Twist UV coordinates and see space warp. Layer noise into landscapes. Push materials past taste into queer extravagance.
patterngeneration.description: A complete shader programming curriculum structured around The Book of Shaders. From basic shaping functions through noise and fractals to queer material design. Each lesson builds on the last: shaping → color → shapes → transforms → patterns → randomness → noise → cellular → FBM → simulation → material extravaganza.
learning_objectives: Shaping functions: step(), smoothstep(), sin(), pow() — sculpting gradients
Color spaces: RGB, HSB, mix() — painting with math
Signed Distance Fields: circles, rects, polygons — geometry from equations
Matrix transforms: translate, rotate, scale UV space
Tiling and patterns: fract(), modular arithmetic, Truchet tiles
Pseudorandom on GPU: fract(sin(dot())) and its variations
Value noise, gradient noise, simplex noise — controlled chaos
Cellular noise: Voronoi, Worley — organic tessellation
Fractional Brownian Motion: layered noise, turbulence, domain warping
Reaction-diffusion and DLA: simulation as pattern
Queer material design: leather, latex, oil slick, fur — tactile computation
Extravagance as aesthetic: melted candy, crushed pearl, memory skin — beauty beyond taste
content: Shader_01_Shaping: Shaping functions — step, smoothstep, sin, pow as visual tools

Shader_07_Noise: Noise functions — value, gradient, simplex, warped
Shader_08_CellularNoise: Cellular noise — Voronoi diagrams, Worley noise
Shader_09_FBM: Fractional Brownian Motion — layered noise, turbulence, domain warping
Shader_10_ReactionDiffusion: Simulation patterns — reaction-diffusion, DLA growth
Shader_11_QueerRubber: Queer materials — leather, latex, oil slick, plastic, fur
Shader_12_PinkExtravaganza: Drag shader finale — melted candy, crushed pearl, extreme pink
